$note: THE ACCESSIBILITY CONTRACT. Every foreground/background pair the product actually renders, so contrast becomes decidable instead of a spot check. scripts/check-a11y.mjs scores every row against all 9 schemes x 2 modes and fails the build on any shortfall. A pair that is not listed here is not checked — adding a rendered pair is part of adding a component. See docs/token-engine-architecture.md 2.4.
$rule: An exemption needs a reason, a note and an owner. `exempt` is NOT `pass`: exempt rows are reported and never scored, so a waiver stays visible instead of becoming a silent omission.

$note: Button labels. `label/l` is 14px, so 4.5:1 applies — large-scale text starts at 24px, or 18.66px bold, and only display/xl, heading/2 and heading/3 qualify in this ramp. These four rows are the ones that were failing in 15 of 18 scheme/mode combinations before the foreground became derived.

knownDefect.note: In LIGHT mode the primary ramp spans 500 to 700 — from mid-lightness, which needs dark text, to dark, which needs light text — so NO single label colour clears 4.5:1 on all three fill states. The button does not change its label on hover, so one of the states must fail. 7 of 9 schemes are affected; only Violet and Slate work, because their 500 is already dark enough for white throughout. Dark mode is fine everywhere (fills run 400 to 200, all light). Fixing this means changing the light-mode interaction ramp so hover and pressed stay on one side of the luminance crossover — a brand-visible change needing sign-off, not a code fix.

Same root cause as the hover row above. Note Default light fails on HOVER specifically because the blue ramp is not monotonic — blue-600 #2a7fc1 is lighter than blue-500 — which AGENTS.md §1 already documents as deliberate.

$note: Non-text UI, 3:1 per SC 1.4.11. The focus ring is also SC 2.4.11, and is checked against surface/subtle because that is the hardest light surface it must separate from.

knownDefect.note: action/primary/rest serves two roles: a FILL behind a label (button background) and a FOREGROUND indicator (active nav icon, selected border, ~29 palette.primary.main sites). As a fill it is fine; as an indicator it needs 3:1 against the surface, and Sunset's orange-500 is 2.96:1 on white and 2.60:1 on surface/subtle. AGENTS.md §3b already flags that exact 2.60:1 pairing as logotype-only. The fix is to split the indicator role onto its own derived step — the same treatment focus/ring now gets — which means rewiring those call sites to distinguish fill from indicator. That is M1/M3 work, not a token change.

exempt.note: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component. 2.52:1 light, 2.04:1 dark.
SC 1.4.11 covers user interface components and graphical objects, not separators. Controls that need a visible edge use border/strong, which is scored above.
1.00:1 in dark mode — both resolve to Neutral-800 #333333. Genuinely invisible, which is why panelBorder() exists and picks border/default on dark surfaces. See AGENTS.md section 1.
Separator, not a control. 1.32:1 light, 1.46:1 dark.
